text: All of these will slaughter a multitude of Romans.
They will be gathered together toward the sea.
The number of that people is ten thousand times ten thousand, and a thousand times a thousand,
with other crowds beyond measure and beyond counting.
Ishmael will cry aloud in a great voice, boasting and saying:
Where is the God of the Romans? There is no one to help them, for they have truly been defeated.
Then the three sons of Hagar themselves will roar against the Romans.
Come, let us cross over to Byzantium.
Unable to do so, after taking counsel they will say again:
Come, let us make a bridge from ships and cross over to Byzantium, the Seven-hilled City.

So the most godless and all their enemies will speak. But the rulers of the Seven-hilled City and its nobles, when they hear the threats of the godless and fear that the Christians sealed by holy baptism may be handed over, will take refuge on the islands of the sea.
Great fear, distress, and hardship will come upon the Romans.
The people of the Seven-hilled City will be distressed by the sword.
But listen, brothers: because of their lawlessness, God will permit it,
and the first will pitch his bed opposite Byzantium,
and he will strike, and they will be struck.
Then the rulers of the Romans will blaspheme, saying:
Alas, alas! We have no king either in heaven or on earth.
At this cry, the Lord will turn his mercy toward the Romans and toward their vindication, and he will exact justice from his enemies.
A great sound will come from heaven, a terrible earthquake from the earth, and the voice of angels from heaven.
The Lord will bow his head and pour out his anger upon the sons of Hagar and the irreconcilable people of Ishmael,
and the Lord will take cowardice from the Romans and put it into the hearts of Ishmael, and put the courage of the Ishmaelites into the hearts of the Romans.
The Lord will raise up a Roman king—one whom people say is dead and good for nothing, and whom they suppose died long ago.
For the Lord keeps him in the inland region of Persia and among the Syrians.
His name begins with the letter K of the alphabet.
He will come to the Seven-hilled City toward evening, while preparations are under way.
He will prepare himself against his enemies.
On the Sabbath morning, as the sun rises, he and his two young sons will engage in a great battle with Ishmael and the sons of Hagar.
The rulers and nobles of the Seven-hilled City will fight alongside him.
The leaders and priests of the churches will carry weapons of war.
Then that king, with his two young sons, will wage a fierce war against the people of the sons of Hagar.
He will cut them down like reed grass burning in a fire.
A three-year-old bull will choke in their blood.
The king alone will put a thousand to flight, and the two young sons will rout tens of thousands.
Ishmael and the sons of Hagar will be utterly cut down.
There will be war and great bloodshed, such as has not happened since the foundation of the world.
For blood will mingle with the sea for twelve stadia.
In the streets of the city, horses will be dyed in blood and drown in it.
None of that people and Ishmael will remain except three of their tents.
They will serve the chief helmsmen of the Seven-hilled City for thirty years.
The people of the Romans will long to see even a trace of Ishmael, but will not find one.
For the prophetic word will be fulfilled, which says:
How will one chase a thousand, and two rout ten thousand, unless God has rejected them and the Lord has handed them over?
That king will bring every enemy and adversary under his feet.
The sceptre of his kingdom will endure for a long time, as will those of the two young sons.
His fame will spread from the sunrise in the east to its setting in the west, and from the south to the north.
He will set his sword in the East and his bow on the flanks of the North and the Bear.
No one will withstand his right hand, for he has come from God.
He will establish great peace,
and cities, fortresses, and churches will be built.
Many altars will be set up throughout the inhabited world.
Houses will be established even on the islands.
Grain, wine, and oil will increase.
That sceptre will put an end to every war on earth.
In his kingdom, the war chariots will be turned into sickles, swords, and boring tools.
The rulers of the Romans will wish to wage war but will find no opportunity. That king will be called by a beast's name.
The whole circuit of the earth will fear him.
That king will glorify the God of heaven, because in his reign God gave him good things such as had not been given from the foundation of the world until that time.
He and his two young sons will lie down in peace
after thirty-three years of his reign.
After him a ruler will arise from the North,
committing the gravest lawlessness against God and his holy ones. He will carry out many injustices and commit great lawlessness.
He will join a son to his mother and a father to his daughter.
The full measure of transgression, debauchery, and incest will be reached, as the people indulge according to his decrees.
The sacrifices and hymns to God will cease.
Then God will command, and it will be shaken by heavenly fire.
After him a foul, foreign woman will reign over the Seven-hilled City.
She will take her seat upon the back of the Seven-hilled City.
Then: Woe to you, Seven-hilled Babylon,
for your wealth and your glory will fall,
along with the boast you uttered:

I am clothed in gold, blue cloth, pearls, a scarlet robe, purple, silver, and electrum; and my hand is not [the Greek is unclear here], for kings reign in me, rulers enter and leave, and great lords dwell in me.
Woe to you, wretched Babylon, mother of all cities, for God will turn his wrath, full of fire, upon you.
Your lofty walls will sink beneath the waters.
Nothing will remain in you except one pillar of the great sceptre of Byzantium, of great Constantine, so that those sailing the sea may lament there.

The kingdom will be taken from you. Your merchants will flee from you and vanish, and every city and region will mourn you, mother of cities. For at that time the kingdom will be removed from Byzantium and given to Rome.
A ruler will arise in Judea;
his name is Dan.
He will reign in Jerusalem. The scattered people of the Hebrews, the Jewish race,
will gather there from every city and region,
and come to Jerusalem to their king.
They will oppress the Christians everywhere on earth
and press the Romans to the point of death.
While Dan is reigning, the Antichrist will come out of the depths beneath the Abyss, through the chasms and roaring of the earth.
He will enter a tiny shrimp-like fish,
and rise up in the broad sea.
(He will grow great,) and twelve fishermen will catch him.
The fishermen will become furious with one another.
One of them will gain power over them; his name is Judas.
He will take the fish as his share, come to a place called Gouzith, and sell the fish for thirty silver coins.
A maiden, a virgin, will buy the little fish.
Her name is Adikia, because a son of lawlessness is destined to be born from her.
Her surname will be Destruction.
For when she touches the fish's head, she will be found pregnant, and the Antichrist will be born from her.
He will be born at three months.
He will nurse from her for five months.
He will go to Jerusalem and become a false teacher.
He will appear quiet, downcast, affectionate, and harmless, pursuing lawless deeds.
His full height will be ten cubits,
and the hair of his head will hang down to his feet.
He will have three heads.
His footprint will be three cubits long.
His eyes will be like the star that rises in the morning.
The upper part of his teeth will be iron, and the lower part of his jaw will be diamond.
His right arm will be iron, and his left one bronze.
His left hand will be three cubits long and his right hand four cubits.
He will have a long head and a long nose.
He will have three letters written on his forehead: A, K, T.
A means “I deny,” K means “and I renounce,” and T means “the defiled dragon.”
When the reign of Dan ends, the Antichrist will teach and be taught, test and be tested.
There will be a harvest of grain, wine, and oil such as has not been since the world's foundation. For there will be three periods in which people cultivate the world's good things.
In those days an ear of grain will yield half a palm-measure of wheat.
A vine-skin will put forth a hundred clusters of grapes.
A single cluster will yield abundance and pour out two measures of wine.
The olive berry will be whole, entirely without [the Greek wording about its substance is unclear].
Abundant growth will spring from everything—that is, from every kind of harvest.
The fruitful earth will burst forth with a hundredfold crop. There will be great rejoicing, such as has not been since the world's foundation, until those seasons come.
The Jewish people and the people of Jerusalem will hold a council, saying:
Come, let us make this extraordinary and remarkable man king—the one who has three letters on his forehead.
For he is fit to become king. They will crown him on the third day.
He will reign for three years.
In the third year of his reign, every crop on the face of the earth will fail.
Nothing will be found in the whole world except half a measure of wheat and one jar of wine and oil. No other produce will be found.
Then a severe plague will come,
and those on the mainland will flee to the islands, while those on the islands flee to the mainland.

Disease will spread across the whole earth, span by span and [the Greek word here is unclear], and a great plague will come such as never occurred until that age. The earth will be afflicted by the plague that is to come,
and people's faces will look lifeless.
If the righteous can scarcely be saved then, where will the sinner appear?
Then the unclean spirits and demons will come out from their places in the Abyss, among the cliffs, in the depths below, in caves, lakes, springs, baths, and the air.
They will come out like the sand of the sea and attach themselves to the Antichrist. They will test people and kill women's infants,
and suck the milk from women.
Then people will call for death, open the graves of the dead, bless the dead, and say:
Blessed—yes, three times blessed—are you who died before us, because you did not live to see these last, harsh, utterly wicked days.

They will plead with the mountains, saying, “Cover us, mountains!” and say to the sea, “Holy sea, let the fury of your currents swallow us!” Woe to the women nursing children and to those who are pregnant in those most wicked days.
Then all the flesh of the Romans will lament,
while the Jews will have great joy and gladness, and the Christians will suffer distress and anguish because of the oppression of the evil demons and the coming plague.
The earth will be worn away and become like copper-colored sand.
Every plant (all grass too) will dry up,
and every tree and every flower (of grass) on the earth will disappear.
The harbors and rivers will dry up,
and wells and every moist source of water will dry up. People's faces will look dead because of the coming plague.
Then the Antichrist will take stones in his hands, crying out and saying:
Believe me, and I will make the stones into bread.
Then the Jews will bow down to him, saying:
You are the Christ whom we await, and because of you the Christian people have grieved us. Then the Jews will rejoice greatly, speaking these words with the Antichrist.
Then the Antichrist will boast greatly to the Jews, saying:
Do not grieve like this.
In a little while the Christian people will see who I am. The day will test you, and I will put you to the test.
Then the Antichrist will raise his voice to the sheer rock, saying, “I made heaven and earth. I speak to you, sheer rock:
Become bread before the Jews!”
But the rock will disobey him and become a dragon.
The dragon will cry out and speak to the Antichrist:
O worker of every kind of lawlessness, filled with every injustice! Why do you claim to do what you cannot do?
The dragon will put him to shame before the Jews.
Then three men will come out to expose him (and convict him as a liar and deceiver):
two from the clouds of heaven and one from the earth. They will go ahead of the Antichrist, reproaching him and saying:
Woe to you, lawless one, worker of injustice and heir of eternal darkness!
They will proclaim it throughout the whole earth, crying out to the afflicted Christians:
Listen, children of humanity; do not worship him. He is neither the Christ nor a God-fearing man; he is the Antichrist.
Many Christians will run to the feet of the holy ones, saying:
What should we do, holy ones?
Where can we Christians hide?
At their words many Christians will hide in mountains, caves, and holes in the earth, and will be saved, so that the deceitful Samuel will not catch them.
When the Antichrist finds the three heralds in the midst of the altar, he will kill them with a sword.
Then what was spoken by the prophet David will be fulfilled:
Then they will bring calves up to your altar.
While the Antichrist reigns, demons swarm in disorder, and the Jews devise futile plots against the Christians, the great day of the Lord draws near.
Then judgment and requital will come.
The devil's deception will fall,
and the light of the world will shine forth: Christ our God, the King of glory, to whom all glory, honor, and might are due forever. Amen.
